verdict.rationale: Kong Gateway ships Event Hooks, a first-party entity that listens for specific entity events (create, delete or modify on Services, Admins and similar) and triggers webhook, custom-webhook, log or Lambda (custom Lua) handlers, so the product directly lets users define event-triggered automatic actions. The documented scope is limited to on-prem Gateway entity-change events with a fixed set of handler types. Notification Hub only alerts by email or in-app, and audit-log webhooks only stream logs, so neither adds general rule-based automation. missing for 10: event sources beyond admin entity CRUD (e.g. traffic or runtime events), documented conditional rule logic or filtering, equivalent rule-trigger automation in Konnect SaaS, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can define rules that trigger actions automatically on events

citations.quote: An Event Hook is a Kong Gateway entity that can be configured to listen for specific events from Kong Gateway entities. An Event Hook can be configured to send information to logs, webhooks, or third-party applications.
